# PR-head worktree narration: three variants

I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace. The caller passed resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` instead of Steps 0 and 1.

## Shared prefix (A, A-no-worktree, B)

**Inputs**
- Ordered admitted array, home first: #12 `fix/retry` @ `aaaaaaa…`, then MEMBER_HEADS #13 `fix/cap` @ `bbbbbbb…` and #14 `fix/retry-docs` @ `ccccccc…`.
- All three are in acme/widget, open, target `main`, and have `isCrossRepository=false`.
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.

**Root and home**
1. Run `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` from the session cwd. The common dir is `/work/widget/.git`, so `ROOT=/work/widget`.
   - In B the session's git-dir is `/work/widget/.git/worktrees/other`. That linked tree is never adopted, and caller HEAD `9999999` is ignored.
2. Run `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree`. It prints nothing, so this is not a submodule.
3. There is no overrides file, wrapper or native tool, so the default home applies. `<name>=fix-retry` and the home is `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.

**Fetch and remote checks**
4. Run `git -C /work/widget fetch origin`. It succeeds.
5. For each admitted PR, run `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q <oid>^{commit}` and `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/<branch>`. All three objects exist, and each `origin/<branch>` equals its supplied head.
6. Run `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main`, giving `BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`.

**Ordered stops**
7. Fork check: no PR is fork-hosted, so this stop does not fire.
8. Run `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain`. `fix/retry` is not checked out at any path other than the selected home, so this stop does not fire.
9. Reachability check: already passed in step 5.
10. The N=1 local-branch ancestry row does not apply (N=3).

**Interrupted-merge recovery check** (a local `fix/retry` exists in every variant)
11. Run `git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry`. This inspects the actual local home tip, never caller HEAD. Result: `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee` in A and A-no-worktree, `2222222…` in B.
12. Run `git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa <local tip>`. It exits 0.
13. Run `git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..<local tip>`.

## Variant A: existing clean home

**Validate the recovered history**
- Step 13 returns one entry: `eeee… aaaa… bbbb… merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12`.
- It has two parents.
- The subject is canonical.
- #13 is an admitted member, `bbbbbbb` matches its original head, and the second parent is the full original `bbbb…`.
- Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain`. Output is empty, so the tree is clean.
- Recovery is valid. #13 is skipped and recorded as `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`. No new commit is made.

**Provision**
- I use the row "List recovery validated an existing home branch": reuse the selected worktree unchanged. There is no reset, update-ref, `-b`, clean, or deletion.
- Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD`. It equals the validated tip `eeee…`.

**Member merges**
- #13 is skipped (already landed).
- #14:
  - Save the last-good SHA: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` gives `eeee…`.
  - Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`. It merges cleanly as `fffffff`.
  - Record `Member merge: #14 fffffff`.

**Base merge**
- Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main`. It produces a clean merge, recorded as `merge: 1111111`.

**Provenance proof**
- Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor <oid> HEAD` for `aaaa…`, `bbbb…` and `cccc…`. All exit 0.

**Step 4 read-back**
- `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` lists `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
- `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry branch --show-current` prints `fix/retry`.

**Report**
```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Ready to implement retry-cap rework
```
MEMBER_HEADS are carried to gather. No push, close, spec or plan writes.

## Variant A-no-worktree: branch exists, no worktree

**Validate the recovered history**
- Steps 11–13 give the same results as A: local tip `eeee…`, ancestry exit 0, and one valid canonical #13 merge entry.
- The step 8 worktree list shows no checkout of `fix/retry` anywhere, so there is no tree to dirt-check.
- Record `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`.

**Provision**
1. Fresh-creation source check: run `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain`. It is empty, so the source is clean.
2. Home-safety check: run `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees`. It succeeds, so `.worktrees` is already ignored and no `.gitignore` commit is needed.
3. Recovery row: run `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry`.
   - This checks out the existing branch.
   - There is no `-b`, update-ref, reset, or deletion.
4. Run `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD`. It equals the validated local tip `eeee…`.

**Merges, proof and report**
- The #14 merge (last-good `eeee…`, giving `fffffff`), the base merge (`1111111`), the three ancestry proofs and the Step 4 read-back are identical to A.
- The report is identical to A's.

## Variant B: refusal before any write

**Validate the recovered history**
- Step 11 inspects `refs/heads/fix/retry`, not session HEAD `9999999`. The tip is `2222222…`.
- Step 12 ancestry from `aaaa…` exits 0.
- Step 13 returns two entries: the valid #13 merge `eeeeeee`, then `2222222`.
- `2222222` has a single parent and the subject `unrelated cleanup`. It is not a member merge from this list, so recovery fails.

**Stop before any worktree write**
Nothing is created, merged, reset, rebased or deleted. The stop names the selected home path:

> `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry on fix/retry carries commits beyond PR #12's head (aaaaaaa) that are not member merges from this list; resolve by hand or remove the worktree.`

The skill ends here: there are no member or base merges and no Step 4 report.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
I’m using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

All commands below are synthetic. **Every command’s cwd is `/work/widget`**; the process cwd never changes. The three variants are independent.

## Shared preflight

Resolved caller values:

- `ROOT=/work/widget`
- Home PR: `acme/widget#12`
- `BRANCH=fix/retry`, `NAME=fix-retry`
- `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- Members, in order: #13 at `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, then #14 at `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`
- Base ref: `main`

Commands, in order:

```bash
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
```

The caller root is the primary checkout, not a submodule. Even in B, I do not adopt the session’s unrelated linked worktree.

Configuration discovery checks these paths in order:

```bash
ls /work/widget/.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md /work/widget/gauntlet-overrides.md /work/widget/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md
ls /work/widget/.pi/settings.json /work/widget/AGENTS.md /work/widget/script /work/widget/bin
```

The stipulated configuration supplies no applicable overrides or wrapper. The selected home remains `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.

```bash
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
```

All three original objects exist; each remote equals its admitted head. Resolve:

`BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`

All PRs are in-repository. No branch is checked out at a conflicting path. The single-PR local-ancestor rule does not apply to this three-PR recovery.

## A — existing selected worktree

Inspect the **local home branch**, not caller HEAD:

```bash
git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry status --porcelain
```

The tip is `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`. The sole intervening commit has exactly the supplied two parents and canonical #13 subject. The selected tree is clean. Recovery is valid: reuse it unchanged; #13 has already landed.

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse --short=7 HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse --short=7 HEAD
```

The initial HEAD equals the validated local tip. The new member merge is `fffffff`; the base merge is `1111111`. No replacement #13 commit is created.

Then run the final checks below.

## A-no-worktree — provision the recovered branch

Run the same local-tip inspection, ancestry check, and first-parent log as A. They validate `eeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee`. No existing selected tree needs a cleanliness check.

Before creation:

```bash
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
test -e /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
```

The source is clean; the selected path is absent, and the ignore check succeeds. No ignore-file write is needed.

Announce: “Setting up an isolated worktree at `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on branch `fix/retry` for this work.”

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
```

HEAD equals the validated local tip. This checks out the **existing recovered branch**, without `-b`, `update-ref`, reset, or deletion.

Run A’s #14 merge, short-HEAD read, base merge, and short-HEAD read, with exactly the arguments shown there. Outcomes are again `fffffff` and `1111111`.

## Final checks and Step 4 report — both successful variants

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry branch --show-current
```

All ancestry proofs succeed; path and branch match.

```text
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Ready to implement retry caps
```

## B — pre-write refusal

After shared preflight:

```bash
git -C /work/widget rev-parse refs/heads/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa refs/heads/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget log --first-parent --format='%H %P %s' aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa..refs/heads/fix/retry
```

The local tip includes ordinary single-parent commit `2222222`, subject `unrelated cleanup`. Recovery fails. Caller HEAD `9999999` is irrelevant.

Stop before writes or merges:

```text
worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry on fix/retry carries commits beyond PR #12's head (aaaaaaa) that are not member merges from this list; resolve by hand or remove the worktree.
```

No Step 4 report is issued for B.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: the recovery check reads refs/heads/fix/retry (explicitly not caller HEAD 9999999), proves ancestry from aaaa…, walks --first-parent %H %P %s after the supplied home head, and checks two parents, canonical subject, admitted member identity and the full original second parent; A records `Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)`, merges #14 then origin/main, and the report lists #12/#13/#14 original heads home first; A-no-worktree adds the selected home with plain `worktree add … fix/retry` (no -b/update-ref/reset) and confirms HEAD equals the validated tip with no invented commit; B stops before any write with the exact message naming the selected path, fix/retry, PR #12's head (aaaaaaa) and the not-member-merges reason. Two small wording points worth tightening so the refusal fact stays unambiguous: in B, After says nothing is created/merged/reset/rebased/deleted but no longer states explicitly 'no spec or plan writes' (Before did in the shared closing line) — add that phrase to the B stop paragraph; and B's step 13 lists the entries as '#13 merge eeeeeee, then 2222222', which inverts git log's newest-first order shown in Before — keep `2222222… eeee… unrelated cleanup` first to match the real walk output. Also note After dropped the Threads fetch/report lines Before carried; if any sibling case checks thread reporting, restore them.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: both variants read refs/heads/fix/retry rather than caller HEAD, prove home ancestry, walk --first-parent %H %P %s after aaaaaaa, confirm the single intervening commit has the two supplied parents and canonical #13 subject, report 'Member merge: #13 eeeeeee (already landed)' without remerging it, merge #14 then origin/main, prove a/b/c ancestry against final HEAD with home listed first, provision the no-worktree variant with a plain `worktree add` (no -b/update-ref/reset), and issue the identical pre-write refusal in B naming the selected path, fix/retry, #12's aaaaaaa, and the not-member-merges reason. Two small drifts worth watching though neither moved a fact here: After's A-variant ancestry check substitutes the literal eeee… for refs/heads/fix/retry (prefer keeping the ref form so the proof is visibly bound to the actual branch tip just read), and After dropped the review-thread fetch and the 'Threads: none' report line entirely — if any thread-related fact is ever added to this case, that omission will fail it, so the Change wording should retain the pr-head-threads step rather than letting the merge-forward/recovery emphasis crowd it out.
